newsitem.title: UK: Wet Brent jumps, confidence rises for Feb barrels.
newsitem.headline: Wet Brent jumps, confidence rises for Feb barrels.

text.p: The North Sea Brent physical market made strong gains on Tuesday as expectations of a fairly tight early February market grew, traders said.
"The market has been sitting on the fence for the last few days or so, but it has made a definite move to the bullish side now," said one North Sea dealer.
A Brent cargo that was nominated from the paper chains on Monday and clocked to a U.S. major was sold on this morning at a strong March Brent +28 cents.
The deal for the Feb 4-6 loader was 15 cents firmer than a March-related Brent deal done on Monday.
"People are thinking that the market might just get a bit tight for the first decade (Feb)," said one trader.
With an open transatlantic arbitrage, more North Sea barrels are expected to move to homes in the United States.
A Wall Street trader has already sold a VLCC of Brent to U.S. Gulf Coast refiners for late Feb delivery at around NYMEX March crude -25 cents, U.S. crude traders said.

A European major is offering barrels from a end-Jan loading VLCC into the U.S., while others are showing cargoes for early March delivery at March NYMEX crude -40/-50 cents. Two Brent dates were to turn wet today from the original Feb programme.

On paper, Brent intermonth spreads firmed, with Feb/Mar traded at a high of +43 cents. Outright levels for March Brent were slightly weaker in line with the IPE screen which was trading nine cents down at $22.49 a barrel at 1319 GMT.
Norwegian grades were valued steady to firmer after two Osebergs, two Statfjords and the last Jan-loading Gullfaks were moved on Monday.
Phillips Petroleum said on Tuesday that the 350,000 barrel per day (bpd) Ekofisk field was restarted at 1240 GMT, after production was shut in for a week when a gas leak was discovered in a pipeline.
